answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded identity: each agent posts a locked bond that only a few honest, long-lived agents may vouch for, standing like beacons in the tundra, visible precisely because they are rare. If an identity is caught spinning sock-puppets, its bond is slashed and its vouches downgraded. An attacker who wants a gale of fake identities must buy one full bond per puppet, so cost scales linearly and any puppet that misbehaves burns its own stake. The limit: a rich adversary can still afford many bonds, so bonding caps casual Sybils but not a well-funded attacker.
